Feasible GLS under heteroskedasticity of unknown form (González-Coya and Perron, 2024)

Source: R/lasso_fgls.R
lasso_fgls.Rd

Shortcut for fgls() with serial = "none". The log of the squared OLS residuals is regressed on candidate covariates z by an adaptive Lasso tuned by cross-validation; the exponentiated fit gives the weights of a weighted least-squares regression. Inference uses the sandwich of eq. (6) with the bias correction of eq. (8), so it remains valid when the skedastic model is misspecified.

Usage

lasso_fgls(
  formula,
  data,
  subset,
  na.action = stats::na.fail,
  hetero = c("lasso", "svr", "wls_s1", "wls_s2", "known", "none"),
  vcov = c("robust", "nonrobust", "HC0", "HC1", "HC2", "HC3", "bootstrap"),
  z = "auto",
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula, as in stats::lm(). Include an intercept unless the model truly has none.

data

A data frame, a list, a ts/mts object, or a 'zoo'/'xts' object containing the variables in the formula. Rows must be in time order (unless serial = "none").

subset

Optional expression selecting rows, evaluated in data. For time series only a contiguous block makes sense.

na.action

stats::na.fail() (default) stops on missing values; stats::na.omit() or stats::na.exclude() drop them. For time series only leading and trailing missing values can be dropped.

hetero

Skedastic-function estimator: "lasso" (default), "svr", "wls_s1", "wls_s2", "known" or "none" (OLS with HC3 standard errors).

vcov

"robust" (default; eq. 8 for Lasso/SVR, eq. 7 for WLS-S1/S2, HC3 otherwise), "nonrobust", "HC0"–"HC3" or "bootstrap" (wild bootstrap).

z

Candidate covariates of the skedastic function: "auto" (default) builds \(\{x, x^2, \log x, (\log x)^2, \cos x, \cos 2x\}\) from every non-constant regressor (see make_dictionary()); a character vector of regressor names; a one-sided formula evaluated in data (e.g. ~ x + I(x^2) + w); or a numeric matrix / data frame with one row per row of data.

seed

Optional seed for the cross-validation folds and the bootstrap. The session's random number generator state is restored afterwards.

...

Further arguments passed to fgls(), e.g. variance, cv_folds, lambda_rule, weight_clip, use_t, control.

Value

An object of class "fgls"; see fgls().

References

Perron, P. and González-Coya, E. (2026). Feasible GLS for time series regression. Journal of Econometrics, 258, 106346. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2026.106346

González-Coya, E. and Perron, P. (2024). Estimation in the presence of heteroskedasticity of unknown form: a Lasso-based approach. Journal of Econometric Methods, 13(1), 29–48. doi:10.1515/jem-2023-0007

Romano, J. P. and Wolf, M. (2017). Resurrecting weighted least squares. Journal of Econometrics, 197(1), 1–19. doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2016.10.003

See also

Other fgls: compare_fgls(), fgls(), fgls-methods, fgls_control(), plot.fgls(), serial_fgls(), summary.fgls()

Other heteroskedasticity: make_dictionary()

Examples

het <- simulate_hetero(200, skedastic = "x2", seed = 1)
fit <- lasso_fgls(y ~ x, data = het, seed = 1)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> lasso_fgls(formula = y ~ x, data = het, seed = 1)
#> 
#> FGLS (hetero); skedastic fit: lasso (selected: x^2, log(x), cos(2x)); covariance: robust
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>      0.9988       1.0157  
#> 
fit$skedastic$selected
#> [1] "x^2"     "log(x)"  "cos(2x)"
ols <- lasso_fgls(y ~ x, data = het, hetero = "none")
compare_fgls(OLS = ols, FGLS = fit)
#>          term statistic       OLS      FGLS
#> 1 (Intercept)  estimate 0.9492108 0.9988174
#> 2 (Intercept) std.error 0.5227244 0.4828889
#> 3 (Intercept)  ci.width 2.0490420 1.8928895
#> 4           x  estimate 1.0142749 1.0157196
#> 5           x std.error 0.2284271 0.2148521
#> 6           x  ci.width 0.8954176 0.8422049
